summary: Sierra National Forest lookout with 1908/09 origins, a 1957 CL-100 steel cab, fire-season staffing and a 3.9-mile hike from Beasore Road.

access.note: Staffed Forest Service lookout. The final approach is on foot; the sources describe the trail but not public entry into the cab.

visit.trail_note: About 3.9 miles round trip, out and back, over exposed granite, starting after a long high-clearance drive up Beasore Road.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Sierra National Forest

events.note: Compass lookout built and hiked to each day, per fire-lookouts.org.
NHLR dates the first structure to 1908/09. Fire-lookouts.org says a compass lookout was built in 1907 and hiked to each day, then a crude lumber cabin in 1908 or 1909.
12-by-12-foot wood cabin similar to the 4A design, per fire-lookouts.org.
4A-type lookout constructed and improved, per fire-lookouts.org.
NHLR says the original lookout was replaced in 1922.
Remodeled with improved windows, per fire-lookouts.org.
Current CL-100 steel cab, 14 by 14 feet, on a 10 by 10 foot concrete block base.
Don Wisseman became a fire lookout; he spent most of his career on Shuteye.
Don Wisseman retired at the end of the 2007 fire season. The page's 20-year service figure does not fit his 1980 start.

corrections.proposed: 1908/09 first structure; current CL-100 steel cab built 1957
corrections.why: The record lists only the first structure. NHLR gives the build history as 1908/1922/1957, and the standing CL-100 cab dates from 1957.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1908/09 for the first structure; fire-lookouts.org says a compass lookout was built in 1907. The story uses the register date and reports the 1907 account.
NHLR lists replacements in 1922 and 1957. Fire-lookouts.org lists changes in 1910, 1915 and 1935 and does not mention 1922. Both date the current cab to 1957.

Fire-lookouts.org says four-wheel drive is required to reach the tower. Wilderness Portal, verified June 2026, describes a 3.9-mile hike after a high-clearance drive on Beasore Road and says the final stretch needs a high-clearance, four-wheel-drive vehicle. Both sources mention four-wheel drive, so the story reports both without ranking them.
The fire-lookouts.org page says Wisseman retired after 20 years, but also gives a 1980 start and a 2007 retirement. The story reports the dates and flags the mismatch.
The record keeps NHLR coordinates (37.349607, -119.428233), which Wilderness Portal (37.3641, -119.4295) roughly matches. Fire-lookouts.org gives 37.2057, -119.25417, about 22 km away; not used.
NHLR gives 8,362 ft (2,549 m); fire-lookouts.org gives 8,358 ft; Wilderness Portal gives 8,355 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.

notes_for_editor: Record kind two_story is not confirmed by these sources; they describe a 14 by 14 foot steel cab on a 10 by 10 foot concrete block base. Staffing as_of uses Wilderness Portal's 2026-06-19 verification date. Fire-lookouts.org's access and staffing details are reported alongside Wilderness Portal's rather than overriding them. No specific fire at the tower is named in the sources read. No photos added: the NHLR photo captions have no image URLs in the pages read.
